title: London Stock Exchange Group plc: Q3 2026 Trading Update
text:
Sustained high growth; strong customer adoption of our AI solutions; raising full-year guidance for revenue growth, EBITDA margins and cash flow; enhancing long-term growth with planned acquisitions of Octus and Trumid
David Schwimmer, CEO said:
“LSEG’s record performance continued in Q3, with accelerating growth across our subscription businesses and sustained performance in Markets. Reflecting this strength, we are raising our full-year guidance for revenue, EBITDA margin and free cash flow. We continue to work with the world’s leading financial institutions as they experiment with, integrate and scale AI across their organisations.
“Our strong cash generation enables us to invest in compelling growth opportunities while also returning capital to shareholders. The planned acquisition of Octus adds valuable proprietary solutions in the high-growth illiquid and private credit space. Alongside the acquisition of Trumid’s innovative credit trading services and our existing scale in liquid credit, we are becoming a global leader in fixed income data and trading.
“Through buybacks and dividends, we will have returned 10% of our market capitalisation to shareholders between January 2026 and February 2027, with capacity for a further £1.0-1.5bn of buybacks in 2027.
"LSEG is on track to deliver its strongest annual growth since 2018, and we continue to invest to further enhance our capacity for sustained, long-term growth and value creation, building a business that is better positioned than ever.”
Q3 2026 highlights
(All growth rates on a constant currency basis unless otherwise stated)
- Strong, broad-based growth: Total income (excl. recoveries) +8.8% (+8.6% year-to-date). Led by Markets +12.5%, FTSE Russell +10.2%, Risk Intelligence +9.8%, and Data & Analytics +5.2%
- Sustained strength in Markets: leading global markets infrastructure benefitting from consistent investment and innovation
- Accelerating subscription businesses 1 : 6.6% growth in subscription businesses in Q3; on track to deliver full year acceleration of c.50bps
- Raising revenue, margin and cash flow guidance: expecting full year growth of at least 8.0%, EBITDA margin expansion of 100-120bps, and equity free cash flow of at least £2.8 billion
- Driving adoption of AI solutions: 95% of top 200 customers using LSEG AI products; more than two-thirds of top 50 customers with MCP connection; expecting a growing contribution to revenues over time
- Enhancing growth with acquisitions of Octus and Trumid: highly complementary businesses, creating a global fixed income leader across the liquidity spectrum
- Returning capital to shareholders: £2.6 billion returned via buybacks this year; current £3.0 billion programme to complete by February 2027; capacity for a further £1.0-1.5 billion in 2027
This release contains revenues, cost of sales and key performance indicators (KPIs) for the three months ended 30 September 2026 (Q3). Constant currency variances are calculated on the basis of consistent FX rates applied across the current and prior year period (GBP:USD 1.318 GBP:EUR 1.168). Organic variance is calculated on a constant currency basis, adjusting the results to remove disposals from the entirety of the current and prior year periods, and including acquisitions from the date of acquisition with a comparable adjustment to the prior year. Certain columns and rows may not add due to the use of rounded numbers.
1. Combined total income (excl. recoveries) of Data & Analytics, FTSE Russell and Risk Intelligence.
Q3 2026: Strong, broad-based growth
LSEG serves its customers through the whole trade lifecycle and data value chain, across multiple asset classes. Trading and data are becoming more intertwined as financial markets grow and increase in sophistication, reinforcing our strategy and strengthening our proposition. The success of this approach is becoming increasingly evident in our financial and operational performance, driving a record financial performance in Q3 and increased expectations for the full year.
Our Markets businesses delivered strong double-digit growth in Q3 and a five year CAGR of over 9%. Continuing macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty complemented the established secular tailwinds from electronification of trading, increasing focus on capital efficiency, and more sophisticated risk management. Our track record of investing in our core, market-leading franchises like SwapClear and Tradeweb, driving scale and growth in established businesses like ForexClear and CDSClear, and innovating for customers in new areas like Post Trade Solutions and Digital Markets, delivers multiple drivers of long-term growth.
Our subscription businesses – Data & Analytics, FTSE Russell and Risk Intelligence – accelerated in Q3, up 6.6%. We continue to see broad demand across Data & Analytics, with particularly good traction in areas of recent investment including cloud-based solutions and our expanded private market content. In October we announced a partnership with NVIDIA, enabling customers to reduce processing of our Tick History data from hours to seconds. As indicated at H1, FTSE Russell re-accelerated and Risk Intelligence continued to deliver strong growth and powerful new solutions.
Record Q3 financial performance reflects the multiple levers of growth the Group has and the significant progress we have made both in transforming individual businesses and in combining them to create additional opportunities. Our upgraded guidance puts us on track to deliver the strongest organic annual revenue growth since 2018 and c.400bps of cumulative EBITDA margin expansion over the last three years.
Successful customer adoption of AI solutions; multi-year monetisation
Our comprehensive, accurate and proprietary data powers business-critical systems for most of the world’s leading financial institutions. With customer trust built up over decades and a history of openness in the way we operate, we are the natural partner of choice for the world’s largest buyside and sellside institutions, among others, as they experiment with, integrate and scale AI across their organisations. The adoption of AI represents a significant long-term opportunity for LSEG and our customers, which we anticipate will drive demand for data, and the associated growth in revenue, for the long-term.
We made significant progress in delivery of our AI strategy in Q3:
- Connecting LSEG Everywhere – Our large customers increasingly access our AI-ready data via multiple distribution channels including APIs, cloud platforms, MCP servers and traditional bulk feeds. Over two-thirds of our top 50 Data & Analytics customers have now connected to our MCP servers, and consumption through this channel for all users grew 5x quarter-on-quarter in Q3. We continue to expand the data and services made available through MCP, with additional datasets including transcripts, fixed income indices and risk models, and we remain on track to have the majority of our data available by year end. We also continue to take advantage of new distribution opportunities for our data, expanding our partnership with OpenAI in Q3, ensuring our data is available wherever customers choose to consume it.
- Driving adoption of transformational products – We rapidly scaled customer adoption of our Workspace AI solutions in Q3, ending the quarter with 47,000 AI Search users, up 30,000 from our H1 results in mid-July. Customer feedback is strong and engagement continues to grow, with average queries per user up 30% in Q3. AI Search is also now available in Microsoft Teams. We have also expanded our premium Workspace AI offering, Deep Research, leading to a 60% increase in usage during Q3.
- Commercialising customer engagement – Consistent with the approach outlined previously, our strategic priority remains driving customer adoption of our AI solutions and embedding our content in new AI distribution channels and agents. Customer engagement remains high with a 50% quarter-on-quarter increase in the number of commercial conversations involving AI in Q3 and consistent with the commercial model laid out in our H1 results.
- Enhancing the value of our broader Data & Analytics business – 80% of the AI agreements struck with customers thus far involve the purchase of additional datasets, illustrating how AI is enhancing our existing offering, opening up new distribution channels, and demonstrating how our Data & Analytics business is more valuable in an AI world.
Creating shareholder value through active capital allocation
The highly cash generative nature of our business gives us significant flexibility in capital allocation. We regularly assess acquisition opportunities, and we return surplus capital to shareholders subject to leverage and other considerations.
Acquisitions
In a separate release today, we are announcing that we have agreed to acquire Octus for a cash consideration of $3.535 billion. Octus is a leading provider of credit solutions, serving customers across private, illiquid and distressed credit. The acquisition will transform LSEG’s presence in credit and private markets data, creating a leading proposition in these high-growth areas. Combining Octus’ capabilities with LSEG’s fixed income data, analytics and distribution means customers will benefit from an integrated view of public and private credit intelligence, enabling them to source deals, assess risk and manage their portfolios through LSEG’s platform.
Earlier this week, Tradeweb announced that it had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Trumid, an electronic credit trading marketplace, for a net purchase price of approximately $1.75 billion. Tradeweb and Trumid have highly complementary trading protocols and the combined suite of credit trading products will further differentiate Tradeweb’s multi-asset class platform, in part by expanding into earlier stages of the bond lifecycle.
These two acquisitions are not only highly complementary to LSEG’s and Tradeweb’s existing businesses, they will also accelerate LSEG’s strategy in fixed income, building a global leader in intelligence, data, workflows and trading across the entire credit liquidity spectrum.
Share buybacks
We repurchased £500 million of LSEG shares in Q3, taking our cumulative buybacks so far this year to £2.6 billion. Under our current programme we expect to repurchase a further £0.8 billion in Q4 and Q1 2027, concluding by February 2027, with the final tranche expected to start in the coming weeks. We have capacity for further share buybacks of £1.0-1.5 billion in 2027.
Consistent with previous guidance, we expect to end the current financial year around the middle of our 1.5-2.5x net debt to adjusted EBITDA leverage range. On a pro forma basis including the transactions and buyback programmes above, we anticipate ending 2027 around the upper end of our 1.5x-2.5x leverage range, before returning to the middle of that range by the end of 2028.
Further raising 2026 outlook, reflecting Q3 momentum and current operating environment
Following the continued strength of our business in Q3, we are further raising our guidance as follows:
- Organic constant currency growth in total income excluding recoveries is now expected to be at least 8.0% , (initial guidance of 6.5-7.5%, raised to 7.0%-7.5% at H1). This combines an acceleration in our subscription businesses’ organic growth and continued strong growth in our Markets division
- An improvement in constant currency EBITDA margin of 100-120 basis points (initial guidance of 80-100 basis points, raised to around 100 basis points at H1)
- Equity free cash flow of at least £2.8 billion , up from previous guidance of £2.7 billion. Both are based on foreign exchange rates of £1 = $1.32 and €1.17
- Capex intensity of c.9.5% of total income excluding recoveries
- Underlying effective tax rate of 24-25%

Rates volumes grew strongly, up 34%, benefiting from shifting interest rate expectations and increased customer activity across government bonds and rates derivatives. Credit also performed well, with volumes up 45%, reflecting continued adoption of electronic trading protocols driving record activity in US investment-grade credit markets.

- OTC Derivatives was up 16.7%, with strength across our suite of clearing solutions, particularly SwapClear which continued to benefit from elevated clearing volumes and strong customer activity. - Group cost of sales grew by 1.1%, benefitting from the revised SwapClear revenue surplus share agreement struck in 2025. Excluding this, cost of sales would have grown at 12.0%, reflecting business mix and the continued investment in content and data capabilities supporting our product offering.
- Gross profit was up 9.9%, ahead of growth in Total Income (excl. recoveries) as a result of the lower growth in cost of sales.

title: LSEG to acquire Octus, creating market leader across public and private credit solutions
text:
NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION, IN WHOLE OR IN PART, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY, IN OR INTO OR FROM ANY JURISDICTION WHERE TO DO SO WOULD CONSTITUTE A VIOLATION OF THE RELEVANT LAWS OR REGULATIONS OF SUCH JURISDICTION
This Announcement contains inside information within the meaning of Article 7(1) of the assimilated Regulation No. 596/2014 as it forms part of the law of the United Kingdom by virtue of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018, as amended and supplemented.
LSEG TO ACQUIRE OCTUS CREATING MARKET LEADER ACROSS PUBLIC AND PRIVATE CREDIT SOLUTIONS
LSEG (London Stock Exchange Group plc) today announces that it has agreed to acquire Octus, a leading provider of credit intelligence, data and workflows, for a cash consideration of $3.535 billion from funds advised by Permira, and Octus’ management, including its founder, Kent Collier. The acquisition of Octus will transform LSEG’s presence in credit and private market data, creating a leading proposition in these high-growth areas. Combining Octus’ capabilities with LSEG’s fixed income data, analytics and distribution means customers will benefit from integrated solutions and intelligence across public and private credit enabling them to source deals, assess risk and manage their portfolios through LSEG’s platform.
About Octus
Founded in 2013 by Kent Collier, Octus is a leading provider of credit solutions across intelligence, data and analytics, serving customers across private, illiquid and distressed credit. Headquartered in New York City and with a global footprint, it has over 900 employees, 750 customers and more than 40,000 individual users including buy-side firms, investment banks, law firms and advisory firms.
Octus’ proprietary data covers the full credit lifecycle, with a leading position in illiquid credit. Its offering includes intelligence, fundamental data and expert analysis that is uniquely developed by Octus’ teams, who source hard-to-access credit documentation, including covenants and deal terms, and turn it into structured, searchable data. Its data is integrated into its purpose-built workflow and portfolio management tools, adding further proprietary data and information for credit market participants. Customers connect to data and insights directly via Octus’ platform, an MCP connector or via AI workflows.
In 2026 Octus is expected to generate over $300 million in revenue, with strong double-digit growth and an adjusted EBITDA margin of around 40%. It has achieved double-digit compound growth in revenue since 2022.
Strategic rationale
Octus’ product set and customer coverage are highly complementary to LSEG’s existing fixed income products. LSEG already has a significant presence in the liquid credit space, through news (IFR), evaluated pricing and corporate actions, and analytics (Yield Book and LPC). Octus brings leading specialism and capability in illiquid and private credit, creating a single source of fixed income data & analytics and workflow spanning the entire credit spectrum. In addition, Octus has a very strong buyside customer footprint, particularly with hedge funds and alternative investment managers, where LSEG has historically been under-penetrated.
Octus significantly expands LSEG’s fixed income offering. LSEG is becoming a leading end-to-end credit data, analytics and workflow provider, supporting customers at every stage of the credit lifecycle, across the full public and private credit continuum. Through LSEG’s existing data and analytics capabilities and the acquisition of Octus, alongside Tradeweb’s planned acquisition of Trumid, LSEG is creating a global leader in fixed income and credit.
Public and private credit markets are converging, with the private credit industry having grown substantially in recent years to an estimated size of $3.5 trillion. The private markets data, workflow and access solutions served market segment is currently $7-9 billion and is expected to grow at a double-digit rate, underpinned by private markets AUM growth and customer demand for timely, accurate and predictive intelligence, and proprietary data and analytics in this less liquid market segment.
The transaction will unlock attractive synergies, both immediate and longer term, as LSEG builds differentiated solutions for customers. There is significant opportunity to drive sales of Octus’ intelligence and workflow solutions across LSEG’s global footprint, and to bring LSEG’s products to Octus’ credit- and buy-side-focused customers. LSEG will also develop enhanced products, combining Octus’ proprietary content with Workspace, LPC, Yield Book, PRS and Tradeweb, to help customers develop a consistent view of a fragmented market with a common data structure, valuation and portfolio management tools.
Upon completion, Octus will be part of LSEG’s Data & Analytics division, with Kent Collier, Founder and CEO of Octus continuing to run the Octus businesses, reporting to Gianluca Biagini and Ron Lefferts, Co-Heads of Data & Analytics.
David Schwimmer, CEO, LSEG, said: “Combining Octus’ leading proprietary data and intelligence with LSEG’s data and analytics business creates a powerful offering for our customers, and further accelerates our growth. Acquiring Octus enables LSEG to deliver best-in-class credit data, intelligence and workflows, across the liquidity spectrum, to a broader range of customers. LSEG’s existing data and analytics capabilities, alongside the acquisition of Trumid announced by Tradeweb and now the acquisition of Octus, position LSEG as a global leader in fixed income to partner with our customers throughout the trade lifecycle. I look forward to partnering with Kent and the team at Octus to continue to drive future growth.”
Kent Collier, CEO, Octus, said: “I’m excited by the prospect and opportunity of Octus becoming part of LSEG. Octus’ customer-first mindset and drive to deliver the absolute best products to our clients is a natural cultural fit with LSEG. Joining LSEG will pair our data, intelligence and workflows with global distribution and fixed income depth: a combination that provides tremendous opportunity for further growth and expansion.”
Financial effects
The transaction is expected to be immediately accretive to LSEG’s Data & Analytics organic revenue growth, and additive to LSEG’s guidance for Group organic subscription revenue growth of around 7% in 2027. Due to Octus’ strong margin profile and operating leverage, there is no change to LSEG’s medium-term guidance for underlying EBITDA margin to increase by a cumulative c. 150 basis points 2027-2029 from the 2026 baseline. The transaction will be neutral to Adjusted EPS in the first full year after completion, and accretive thereafter. The acquisition will be financed by external debt.
Allowing for forecast cash flow, the completion of the current £3 billion share buyback programme by February 2027, the completions of the Octus and Trumid acquisitions, and capacity for further share buybacks of £1-1.5 billion, we expect leverage at the end of 2027 to be around the upper end of the target range of 1.5-2.5x, before returning to the middle of the range by the end of 2028.
The transaction is expected to close in H1 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

David Schwimmer, CEO said:
“LSEG’s record performance continued in Q3, with accelerating growth across our subscription businesses and sustained performance in Markets. Reflecting this strength, we are raising our full-year guidance for revenue, EBITDA margin and free cash flow. We continue to work with the world’s leading financial institutions as they experiment with, integrate and scale AI across their organisations.
“Our strong cash generation enables us to invest in compelling growth opportunities while also returning capital to shareholders. The planned acquisition of Octus adds valuable proprietary solutions in the high-growth illiquid and private credit space. Alongside the acquisition of Trumid’s innovative credit trading services and our existing scale in liquid credit, we are becoming a global leader in fixed income data and trading.
“Through buybacks and dividends, we will have returned 10% of our market capitalisation to shareholders between January 2026 and February 2027, with capacity for a further £1.0-1.5bn of buybacks in 2027.
"LSEG is on track to deliver its strongest annual growth since 2018, and we continue to invest to further enhance our capacity for sustained, long-term growth and value creation, building a business that is better positioned than ever.”

LSEG Q3 2026 Trading Update - Acquisition of Octus
Presentation Transcript
22 October 2026 2
Moderator:
Good morning and welcome to the LSEG Q3 results. At this time, all participants are in listen-only mode.
Later, we will conduct a question and answer session through the phone lines and instructions will follow
at that time. I would like to remind all participants that this call is being recorded. I'll now hand over to
David Schwimmer, CEO of LSEG and Michel-Alain Proch, CFO, to begin the presentation. Please go ahead. 3
David Schwimmer:
Good morning. Thanks for joining the call. I'm here with MAP, our CFO, and Peregrine, Head of Investor
Relations. We continue to deliver very strong growth. Revenue is up 8.8% in the third quarter and 8.6%
year to date. All our businesses are contributing to this growth. Markets continues its outstanding year
with our sustained investment, ensuring it's well positioned to help customers navigate the ongoing
economic and political uncertainty. Our subscription business has accelerated, growing at 6.6% in Q3, up
from 6.3% at H1, and on track to deliver 6.5% for the full year. We are raising 2026 guidance again to
reflect this continuing strength. We now expect full year revenue of at least 8%, putting us on track for
the strongest year of growth since 2018. We're also raising our guidance for EBITDA margins and cash
generation. MAP will walk you through those in a moment. Taken together, our revised guidance speaks
to a business that is growing faster, is more profitable, and is generating more cash than anticipated at
the start of the year.
Our strongcash generationgives ussignificantflexibility incapitalallocation,combining bolt-onM&Aand
significant cash returns to shareholders. I've spoken before about the culture of innovation we've
embedded at LSEG and the pace of product development this is driving. Last week, we announced a
partnershipwithNvidiathatwillreducethetimeforcustomersto analyzeourmassivetickhistorydataset
from days to minutes. And last month, we launched World-Check Resolve, a new AI layer, which reduces
false positives by around 75% and saves our customers a lot of manual checking. Where we have these
leading positions, we continue to invest to maintain that gap and drive growth. On AI, we're driving
adoption at scale. 95% of our top 200 customers are now using our AI solutions. I'll come back to this in a
moment. As you will have seen, we have had two really exciting developments this week.
On Monday, Tradeweb announced its acquisition of Trumid, a high growth electronic credit trading
marketplace. Billy and Sarah have already taken investors through the logic of this deal, but I'll recap this
briefly later. And this morning, we have confirmed the acquisition of Octus, a leader in the provision of
credit solutions in the illiquid and private credit space backed by highly proprietary data. This deal fits 4
squarely within our criteriain terms of both strategic fit and financial discipline. It's highly complimentary
to our existing fixed income product suite and enhancing to growth. Much more on that later. Finally, on
capitalallocation,wehavemaderecordreturnstoshareholdersthisyear,returning£3.4billioninthefirst
nine months. With £800 million remaining on our current buyback program in Q4 and Q1 of next year,
we're on track to return around 10% of our market cap in total since January of this year. We also have
capacity for an additional £1-1.5 billion in 2027. 5
We've built a business capable of partnering with customers through the whole trade life cycle and data
value chain across multiple asset classes. Trading and data are evermore intertwined as financial markets
growandincreaseinsophistication,reinforcingourstrategyandstrengtheningourposition.It'sinevitable
that the external environment will evolve, whether that's asset prices, issuance trends, market volatility,
or GDP growth, but the balanced and diversified nature of our subscription and transaction revenues and
our alignment with multiple long-term growth drivers position us to perform well in almost any
environment. You can see the power of this all-weather business model in the steady and accelerating
growth on this slide. 6
Before I hand to MAP, let me update you on the significant progress we're making in the delivery of our
AIsolutionsandhowthey'reresonatingwithourcustomers.You'llrecallourfocusforthisyearwasrolling
out solutions and driving customer adoption. With 95% of our largest customers using at least one of our
AI solutions and 80% of our top 50 customers using two or more, we've made real progress in driving
adoption in Q3. We had 47,000 users of Workspace AI Search at the end of Q3 and have just passed the
50,000 mark. User engagement with the product also continues to deepen with the average queries per
user up 30%. Crucial to the success are the ongoing enhancements we're making, including scheduled
queries through Microsoft Copilot, a bespoke library of user prompts, and greater export functionality.
LSEG everywhere continues to build. Over two thirds of our largest customers and over 300 in total have
now connected or are onboarding to our MCP.
But our customer engagement on enterprise AI goes far beyond just MCP. As highlighted at the first half,
customers increasingly want to accessour AI ready data viamultiple distributionchannels, including APIs,
cloud platforms, and traditional bulk feeds. Overall, we saw a 50% increase in AI related commercial
discussions in Q3, and 80% of AI license sales involved the customer buying new or additional data sets.
With new AI distribution channels, our customers want more of our data. AI is enhancing the value of our
data, showing that our Data & Analytics business is more valuable in an AI world. With that, let me hand
over to MAP to take you through our financial performance in more detail. 7
Michel-Alain Proch:
Thankyou,David,andgoodmorningto allofyou.Asyoujustheard,wedeliveredanotherstrongfinancial
performance in the third quarter, organic revenue up 8.8%. Data & Analytics was up 5.2% as our ongoing
innovation and investment in content drives demand across our solutions. Data and feeds continue to be
particularly strong, up 7.5%. FTSE Russell was up 10.2% with subscription revenues re-accelerating as we
said it would. We continueto see sustained demand for our screening and identity verification services in
Risk Intelligence, which grew 9.8% in Q3. Taken together, our subscription businesses grew 6.6%, a good
acceleration from the 6.3% in the first half. Our Markets division is sustaining its very strong performance
up over 12% with strengths across all the businesses. OTC derivatives was the standout performer with
continued strengths at SwapClear and almost 30% growth in client volumes in Q3. We continue to work
with the industry to drive adoption of our Post Trade Solutions for uncleared OTC products, signing four
new members to TradeAgent in the quarter. Tradeweb also grew strongly, benefiting from sustained
innovation and investment against the backdrop of shifting interest rate expectation. That drove 22%
growth in volumes in Q3. Finally, cost of sales grew below revenues benefiting from the change to the
SwapClear agreement we made at the end of 2025. As a result, we delivered almost 10% growth in gross
profit for the quarter. 8
Turning to our subscription revenues, we are well on track to deliver full year subscription growth of
around 6.5%, an acceleration from the 6% growth in 2025. These revenues are highly recurring, typically
around 93% annually, and that brings good visibility. New sales made in previous quarters feed through
to revenues once a product is installed and activated, and we have a good line of sight to these timelines
too.
The ongoing investment we make into content capabilities and distribution is reflected in product pricing
and annual increase in LSEG Data Access agreements representing 18% of D&A revenues. And over time,
AI revenues will make a growing contribution to these subscription revenues with a long runway for
growth. 9
Turning now to our Markets division, which has seen another outstanding quarter, volume interest rate
swaps on our trading and clearing platforms were very strong in Q3 as customers turn to our solution
amidst economic and political uncertainty. These dynamics also supported strong volumes across Fixed
Income, Equities and FX, as you can see on this slide. Putting market conditions to one side and taking a
long-term view, these are leading businesses with strong structural growth drivers. Our sustained
investment is helping drive this growth by developing new solutions and expanding reach. Through this
strategy, we have delivered a five-year CAGR of over 9%. 10
Turning to our full-year guidance, most of which we are raising once more. On revenues, we expect
organic revenue growth in2026 to be at least 8%. This is a meaningful increase to the guidance we issued
at H1. We are raising our margin guidance again, expecting between 100 and 120 basis points of
improvement thisyear.This reflectsour continued strong topline performance and our focus onefficient
management and delivery of operating leverage. We reiterate our CapEx guidance at 9.5%, and finally,
our guidance for free cash flow that already reflected the highly cash generative nature of our business
model, but we think we can do even more this year and now expect equity free cash flow to be at least
£2.8billion. AsDavidsaidearlier,our strongcash generation isallowing usbothto executeonM&A when
it makes sense and return cash to shareholders. 11
And you can see on this slide that we have returned a record amount of capital to shareholders this year,
and we are on track to return around 10% of our market capitalization in a little over 12 months. With
that, I will hand back to you, David. 12
David Schwimmer:
Thanks, MAP. I'll now spend a few minutes focusing on the Octus acquisition. We are really excited about
this transaction. It's a great business and the timing is excellent given the work we have done already to
transform our data platform and scale up in fixed income and private company data. I'll explore all of
these points in more detail, but to summarize here, Octus is a leading provider of credit solutions with a
focus on illiquid and private credit. Its data is highly proprietary. Its financial track record is outstanding
with very strong growth and improving margins in a market which will continue to grow at a double-digit
rate. Our margin guidance is unaffected by this deal. Octus coverage and customer footprint are highly
complimentary to LSEGs and will unlock significant product and cross-sell opportunities. The transaction
will be accretive to our top line growth and accretive to EPS after 2028, and we are retaining a high class
management team led by Kent Collier.
And as MAP will lay out, this deal fits well in the context of our broader capital allocation strategy. We're
completing ourcurrent £3billion buyback and we believe investing in our sharesat this level continues to
be a good use of capital. We can see capacity for a further £1-1.5 billion of buybacks in 2027, taking us to
the top end of our leverage range a year from now. 13
OctuslooksalotlikeourD&Abusiness,butfocusedonaspecializedassetclass,illiquidandprivatecredit.
For example, distressed debt, leveraged loans and CLOs, and its solutions span the full credit life cycle -
idea generation, deal tracking, detailed analysis, underwriting, and portfolio and risk management tools.
As with D&A, it delivers through feeds, APIs, and workflow platforms. 14
And these solutions are based on differentiated and proprietary data sets. Private credit is not like the
investment grade corporate bond market. Documentation can be extremely hard to come back.
Structures can be highly bespoke and complex, and sometimes you have to spend days sitting in
courtroomsfollowinglegalprocesses.Evenaccuratefinancialsonprivatecompaniescanbehardto trace,
as many of you have found over the last few days. Octus has been building up this data and associated
insight andexpertiseforover12years,anditincludesthousandsofcontributoryrecordsfromcustomers,
issuers, and investors, often detailed documents on specific loans. This is just not possible to replicate.
We've done extensive customer due diligence and it is clear from the feedback that Octus solutions are
extremely important for day-to-day research, workflow, and risk management. So like our existing data
assets, this is a business that is becoming more valuable in an AI world, and Octus has built strong AI
functionality with MCP connectors and its own credit AI platform, bringing proprietary intelligence and
analytics directly into customer workflows.
To giveyouacoupleofstats,justin2026,itsAIplatformhasgeneratedmorethanfourmillionautomated
classifications of complex market data and had half a million tool calls to its MCP. 15
Octus is a high-growth business in a high-growth market. Revenue has grown at a strong double-digit
CAGR since 2022. In fact, it has compounded at a double-digit rate since its inception. Now has over 750
customersand40,000individualuserswithveryhighretentionrates.Theprivatecreditmarketisgrowing
at around 10 to 15% annually. There are more participants every year, and as I just mentioned, greater
deal complexity just drives increasing demand for specialist solutions, and the user base is broadening
from investorsandadvisorsto underwriters,riskmanagers,andcomplianceteams.Aswe'reseeinginour
own business, AI is driving a range of different delivery mechanisms, increasingly delivering Octus
proprietary credit solutions directly into customer workflows. Revenues are currently weighted around
80% to the buy-side and legal profession and around 70% to the Americas. So as I'll cover on the next
slide, that is highly complimentary to LSEG. 16
Let's look at how these businesses will fit together and create opportunities for additional growth.
First, the combination of LSEG's more liquid and public credit coverage combineswith Octus's illiquid and
private focus to give coverage of the full credit spectrum.
Second, we are able to drive a step change in our overall private company's coverage, marrying all the
workwe havedonebuilding our privatecompany dataset withOctus's 95%coverage in the private credit
universe. This will give us leading private markets coverage.
Third,ourbusinesstodayisweightedto thesell-sideandglobalinstitutionswherewehavedeepstrategic
partnerships. We are under-penetrated on the buy-side where Octus excels. This presents a significant
cross-selling opportunity. And similarly, for our respective geographic footprints, we will bring global
distribution for Octus, which until now has been more focused in North America. Now, MAP will spend a
couple of minutes on the financial aspects of Octus and the deal. 17
Michel-Alain Proch:
Yes, David. And on the financials for LSEG, this deal is also highly attractive. We have talked about the
revenue and growth profile. This will be accretive to D&A growth and will of course be incremental to our
7% guidance for our subscription businesses in 2027. It is also already generating really strong margins,
which is a sign of high quality for a business that has achieved such strong growth, and we only expect
those to improve as the top-line growth continues. Octus has a roughly 40% adjusted EBITDA margin and
a strong operating leverage, which is allowing us to confirm the growth EBITDA improvement of 150 bps
over 2027 to 2029 from the 2026 baseline. Putting this together, it is neutral to EPS in 2028 and accretive
thereafter. David, back to you. 18
David Schwimmer:
Thanks, MAP. As you will have seen a couple of days ago, Tradeweb announced its planned acquisition of
Trumid,anelectroniccredittradingplatform.YoucanseehowitfitstogetherwithTradewebonthisslide.
And just as Octus is for LSEG, Trumid is highly complimentary to what Tradeweb does today. It extends

So I appreciate that's a little longer than our usual Q3 presentation, but there are a lot of great things
happeningacrossLSEG.We'redeliveringrecordresultsandraisingfull-yearguidance.We'redrivingstrong
adoption of our AI solutions and expect that to make a growing contribution to revenues. We are driving
an unprecedented pace of innovation across the business. I've spoken to some of this already, but this is
also a good moment to remind you that our Head of Markets, Daniel Maguire and his team will host an

Finally, we continue to invest both organically and where it makes strategic and financial sense through
acquisition to further enhance our customer proposition. Through that strategy, we are building a
business that is better positioned than ever for sustained long-term growth and value creation. And now
MAP and I are happy to take your questions. Peregrine, over to you. 22
Peregrine Riviere:
Thanks, David. As usual, please restrict yourself to one question and maybe there'll be time for you to
come back and ask another at the end. So operator, I'll hand to you. Thanks.
Moderator:
Thank you, Peregrine. And if you would like to ask a question, please signal by pressing star one to raise
your hand and join the queue. And to withdraw your question, press star one again. When called upon to
ask your question, please ensure thatyou use your handset and thatyou are noton mute. Again, starone
to raise your hand. And your first question is from the line of Andrew Lowe of Citi. Please go ahead.
Andrew Lowe:
Hi, thanks for the very detailed presentation. I just wanted to ask on the Octus deal, it fills a gap in your
